main_text.head: Præfatio ad Lectorem.
main_text.p: Non alius de legentium affectu magis sollicitus, temerè prodiit, quam qui se præsentem oculis tuis ingerit, liber. Idque merito; utpote qui cum illos quibus se viæ indicem pollicetur, per Arabiæ, minùs fœlicis, saxa & arenas circumducat, eorum expectare possit fortem, quibus illi qui eorum operâ per loca non ante trita, utuntur, sentibus & viæ asperis offensi, ἀνδρῶν? licet non infidis, convitia rependunt. Verùm ego bonarum mentium candore me consolor, facilè speran s eos qui melioribus detenti in hæc obiter tantùm oculos conjecerint, veniam ejus quo aliis prodesse studuerim, laborìs concessuros, illos autem, quibus hæc etiam studia cordi sunt, bonam

page.notes: The large initial "N" is a woodcut and is read as N. The Greek word after "offensi," is printed as a small Greek fragment that is uncertain; it has been marked [?] and the Greek letters given are a best reading, not a certain one. Line-end "speran s" appears to contain a spacing gap; read as speranȝ is not assumed, the text shows "speran s" as printed. The word "bonam" at the end is partly cut by the page edge, so the final word is read as "bonam" with the last letters doubtful, and it is printed as "nam" in the catchword position. The last line is partly obscured by a shadow at the lower edge. Show-through and the scanner's edge are excluded. The page is a scan with uneven lighting; the decorative border and initial are not transcribed as text.
